questions.key_step: Homogeneous DE gives y=x arccos x, then area by substitution and parts.
questions.justification: Three routine stages (substitution y=vx, constant, integral by parts); nothing unfamiliar. Same chained-routine class as 2023-P2-Q1 (L2).

questions.key_step: Intersect line and parabola, subtract areas.
questions.justification: One standard move, applied once; comparable but simpler than 2021-P1-Q2 (L2).

questions.key_step: Split at x=1 where max{0,ln x} changes, integrate 2^x and ln x.
questions.justification: Routine integrals, but the split and matching alpha,beta,gamma need care; chain of three steps.

questions.key_step: Intersection points then one integral of line minus parabola.
questions.justification: Single familiar move; direct.

questions.key_step: Tangent to the ellipse, integrate line minus ellipse arc and convert sin^-1 to cos^-1.
questions.justification: Numerical answer with an arcsine integral and exact simplification into the stated form; precision risk but no unfamiliar idea.

questions.key_step: Triangle below y=mx equals half of the total area.
questions.justification: Routine chain: total area, triangle area, solve for m; numerical format nudges it above L1.

questions.key_step: Identify the three parabolas, use symmetry and integrate between y=2sqrt(1-x) and the downward parabola.
questions.justification: Needs a correct sketch of three conics and the bounded region; numerical, so no option check.

questions.key_step: Tangent at the given ordinate, then integrate horizontally.
questions.justification: Tangent plus area along y; a few routine steps.

questions.key_step: Split at pi/4 where cos x - sin x changes sign.
questions.justification: Modulus split and trigonometric integrals; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Parabola and line intersect at -2 and 4; one integral.
questions.justification: One standard move, numerical but short.

questions.key_step: Locate max and min of the cubic, split the area at the root x=0 inside the interval.
questions.justification: Derivative test plus a sign-change split; the net-integral trap makes it above L1.

questions.key_step: Two parabolas meet at y=+-1; integrate in y and double.
questions.justification: One standard area between two parabolas.

questions.key_step: Four crossing points of y=3 with the folded curve; integrate horizontally with two integrals.
questions.justification: Option-based but the region (arch plus two pockets) must be identified correctly and the radicals simplified; slip-prone.

questions.key_step: Parabolas meet at x=2; integrate over y and double.
questions.justification: Direct standard area.

questions.key_step: Probability as ratio of areas of triangles formed by the lines.
questions.justification: Two chapters (straight lines and probability) but both routine; few steps.

questions.key_step: Intersection at x=4, integrate parabola minus line from x=1.
questions.justification: Standard with a truncating line x=1.

questions.key_step: Write the modulus function piecewise: trapezoid.
questions.justification: Piecewise sketching of a two-modulus graph then trapezium; routine.

questions.key_step: Area between parabola and chord minus a triangle that must be checked to lie inside.
questions.justification: Multiple pieces (three curves, triangle inside region) and exact arithmetic with radicals.

questions.key_step: Small piece above y=2x from a quadratic area, whole from integration, then ratio.
questions.justification: Numerical; the curve y=2|x| splitting S needs a clear picture and ratio manipulation.

questions.key_step: Integrate x_line - x_parabola over y from -4 to 2.
questions.justification: Direct single-move area with a sideways parabola.

questions.key_step: f(x)=max(|x+1|,|x+5|) switches at x=-3.
questions.justification: Needs the idea that only the extreme points matter; numerical.

questions.key_step: Horizontal width function with one switch at y=2; diamond area 2k^2.
questions.justification: Two regions defined by inequalities, ratio of areas; numerical.

questions.key_step: Astroid pieces: 3/2 of first quadrant, x=sin^3(theta) and Wallis.
questions.justification: Unfamiliar-ish astroid, symmetric reasoning for the 3/2 factor and Wallis evaluation, numerical.

questions.key_step: Circle minus ellipse and ellipse minus circle, subtract the two equations.
questions.justification: Standard areas pi*a^2 and pi*a*b; short algebra.

questions.key_step: min{x+2,4-3x} switches at x=1/2.
questions.justification: Routine piecewise upper boundary.

questions.key_step: Tangents to the parabola meet on the axis at (-3,1); triangle area.
questions.justification: Two tangents and an area; routine chain.

questions.key_step: Integrate y^a and test the options.
questions.justification: Short; testing options makes it direct.

questions.key_step: Folded branch of |x^2-1|; symmetric region.
questions.justification: Modulus plus two pieces; routine.

questions.key_step: Circle completes to centre (-2sqrt3,0) r=4; area as circle arc minus parabola.
questions.justification: Several stages: complete the square, intersect, sqrt(16-y^2) integral with exact surds.

questions.key_step: Region |x| between sqrt(y)/2 and 3 sqrt(y), y up to 4.
questions.justification: Interpreting three inequalities and integrating in y.

questions.key_step: A1=2A2 differentiates to y=2xy', so the curve is y^2=x; then the normal.
questions.justification: Four stages across three chapters (area, differential equation, normal) but each routine.

questions.key_step: Rewrite x=ln(2/y) as y=2e^{-x}; find the three intersections; integrate ln.
questions.justification: Mixed log and exponential boundaries with exact integration; slip-prone.

questions.key_step: Intersect V with circle, triangle plus segment.
questions.justification: Triangle plus segment or a direct arcsine integral; routine.
